description: Helping Hands live viewer: add a toggleable 'average human hand' reference model. Find a real, proportionally accurate 3D hand model online with a license that allows use (e.g. MANO hand model mean shape, or an openly licensed rigged anthropometric hand; check license, record source/attribution), scaled to average adult dimensions. Show it in the three.js viewer with an on/off toggle so grippers can be compared/mapped against a human hand. The fingers must be articulated: controls (sliders and an open/close animation) to bend each finger and the thumb so we can practice fingers opening and closing alongside the gripper. Jake (voice, 2026-10-20): 'include as an option to turn on or off an average human hand, proportionally accurate, a real 3D model from online... so we can map this thing to the human hand. We should be able to articulate the fingers too.'
test_instructions: Open the live viewer, toggle the human hand on: a realistic average-size hand appears next to the gripper at correct scale.
Use the finger controls: each finger and the thumb bend; open/close animates the whole hand.

results.notes: Also (Jake, voice): add a pose where the human hand is holding onto the gripper, posed realistically around its handle/body, so we can see how a hand grips it.

results.identified_issue: Model choice: MANO was rejected because of its license (non-commercial, registration required). The WebXR generic hand is MIT, but it's a generic stylized-realistic mesh, not a statistical mean shape. Its joints are all flat siblings under the Armature (made for joint-by-joint tracking), so human_hand.js does its own forward kinematics: each finger's three bending joints rotate everything after them about the joint's local X axis (WebXR convention: -Z along the bone, +Y dorsal), and a negative angle curls toward the palm (checked visually). The CURL table holds hand-picked full-fist angles. Scaling: uniform, from the wrist joint to the farthest vertex along the wrist→middle-tip axis, set to the ANSUR handlength. I assumed the WebXR wrist joint is close to the wrist crease (stylion); it hasn't been verified against a landmark. Placement: the hand lines up with the bounds of meshes named 'finger' (or the whole model if there are none), its tip Z at max Z, sitting +110 mm in X when beside, so a fist doesn't reach the jaws. That works for Generalist; other families might want a different offset. The hand lives in view.scene, not view.group, so Explode and Open/Close posing don't move it; frame() and alignAll() include it when it's visible. Vendored three r185 GLTFLoader, BufferGeometryUtils and SkeletonUtils into cad/compare/vendor/{loaders,utils} so the relative imports resolve. Not done: finger spread, thumb opposition, a hand-length dimension readout.
results.summary: Added an 'Average human hand' toggle to the live preview: a real MIT-licensed rigged hand, scaled to the ANSUR II average hand length, with a bend slider per finger and thumb, Open/Close, and an option to bend along with the gripper.
results.detailed_description:
There's a new row in the parts list, right under Reference photo, called 'Average human hand'. Tap its eye to turn the hand on. It shows up in the 3D view with its fingertips level with the gripper's fingertips. By default it sits beside the gripper in +X with the palm facing the jaws, so the way the hand closes lines up with the way the jaws close. You can also switch it to sit over the gripper (it goes see-through there).

The controls under the row are: size (average adult 187 mm, average man 193 mm, average woman 181 mm); right or left hand; beside or over; an Open/Close hand button that animates it; and bend sliders for all fingers together, plus one each for the thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. There's also a checkbox, on by default, labelled 'Bend with the gripper's Open/Close'. With it on, the gripper's Close button makes the hand form a fist at the same time, so you can practice the two side by side. Turn the eye off and the hand disappears.

The model: I looked at MANO first. Its license is non-commercial and you have to register to get it, so I didn't use it. Instead I used the W3C WebXR Input Profiles 'generic hand' (MIT, © 2019 Amazon), downloaded from npm @webxr-input-profiles/assets@1.0.20 and unmodified. It's a real skinned mesh rigged on the 25 standard WebXR hand joints. For size I downloaded the ANSUR II public data (4,082 men, 1,986 women) and computed the mean hand length, wrist crease to middle fingertip: men 193.3 mm, women 181.1 mm, and 187.2 mm for the adult average (the plain mean of those two). The mesh is scaled uniformly to that length, so its proportions stay as modelled.

Here is what I checked. As shipped, the model measures 189.7 mm, wrist to middle fingertip. Across the knuckles it's about 79 mm at that length, against ANSUR's average breadth of 83 mm (88 for men, 78 for women). So it's a slightly narrow hand, a few mm under the average breadth. I screenshotted it in headless Chrome open, as a full fist, at 60% over the gripper as a left hand, and following the gripper's Close, in iso, top and side views. The fingers curl toward the palm, and the fingertips line up with the gripper's in the top view.

Limits: the fingers only bend; they don't spread sideways. The thumb flexes but doesn't swing across the palm (no opposition yet). The full fist uses fixed joint angles, about 85/100/70 degrees per finger.

URL presets: ?hand=1 (or right/left), ?curl=0..100, ?handsize=man|woman, ?handat=over. The live preview picks this up on the next publish. I added .glb to what the publisher copies, and Scripts/test_gallery.py now checks the toggle and the sliders (9/9 pass).

summary: The Helping Hands live viewer's average human hand model needs a new pose where the hand grips the gripper. The hand should wrap realistically around the gripper's handle or body so users can see how a hand holds it.

visual.alt: Gripper open beside an open hand; gripper closed beside a fist
